title: Al-Mutaffifin: short measure
hookLine: woe to those who take full measure and give short (83:1–3)
last: AL-INSHIQAQ — RECORD IN THE RIGHT HAND.

cards: You order a large coffee and it arrives two-thirds full. You notice. You pay for a full tank and the pump seems to click off early.
You notice that too. Now flip it. The report padded to look finished.
The hours logged generously. The split bill where your share gets rounded down. Somehow those are harder to see.
It's easy to measure others with a very precise ruler and yourself with a very forgiving one. The surah just before Al-Inshiqaq opens with one word aimed right at that double ruler.

teach.b: Surah eighty-three begins, in Pickthall's words: Woe unto the defrauders. The Arabic is al-mutaffifin, from tatfif, and commentators tie the word to something small, scant, the scrap left at the bottom.
The mutaffif isn't a bank robber. He skims a tiny amount, a pinch off the top, over and over, where nobody can quite prove it. Verses two and three describe him exactly.
When people measure for him, he demands it full. When he measures or weighs for them, he gives less. Same scale, two rulers.
Then verse four asks: do they not think they'll be raised up, on a tremendous day, the day people stand before the Lord of the worlds? A tiny cheat, set next to the biggest day imaginable.

A report in Ibn Majah, from Ibn 'Abbas, says that when the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ came to Medina, its people were among the worst at giving short measure. Then this surah was revealed, and their measuring became good.
Whether or not every detail of that report holds, it shows how the first Muslims heard the surah: as marketplace instruction, practical, not abstract. The Qur'an returns to fair measure elsewhere.

teach.h: FULL FOR ME, SHORT FOR YOU.
teach.b: In Surah Hud, the prophet Shu'ayb tells his people of Madyan: give full measure and full weight, and don't cheat people of what is theirs.
Few people weigh grain at a stall anymore.
But the measuring hasn't stopped: hours, effort, credit, attention, a fair share of the housework.
The market's question still stands. Do you use one ruler for both sides?

how: Honest weights and measures belong to Muslim business ethics; Al-Mutaffifin is recalled as a warning against small, hidden cheating, and in the past market inspectors in Muslim cities checked weights and measures.

o: robbers who take everything by force
those who skim a little off what they give
those who charge high interest on loans

games.q: what's inside the surah — tap the pairs.

s: the mutaffif is a big-time robber
commentators tie the word to something small: he skims a little, often, where it's hard to prove.
a report says Medina's merchants improved after this surah
Ibn Majah, from Ibn 'Abbas: they were among the worst at measure, then became good.
fair measure appears in the Qur'an only in this surah
Shu'ayb's people of Madyan are told the same, give full measure and weight.

games.q: you run a market stall. a customer is buying grain. nobody would notice a pinch less. what does Al-Mutaffifin warn against?
o: demanding full measure for yourself but giving short
games.why: full when they take, short when they give (83:2–3): one ruler for others, another for themselves.

practice: Run through the exchanges coming up today, money, work, time, chores, a favor owed, and find one where you might give a little short and take a little full, where nobody would know.
Picture giving it full measure instead: the full hour, the fair share, the honest number.

wordCard.voice: Al-Mutaffifin. Those who give short measure, the ones who skim a little, and the name of Surah eighty-three. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: "those who give short measure," from t-f-f, a small amount, a little bit.

carryVoice: Your line: full measure. Even a small pinch, where no one is checking, still counts. See you tomorrow.

sources.ref: Qur'an 83:2–6 (full when taking, short when giving; the tremendous day)
Qur'an 11:84–85 (Shu'ayb: give full measure and weight)
Sunan Ibn Majah 2223 (Ibn 'Abbas on the people of Medina)
